title: Socratic checklist — manuscript writing & reporting (写作与报告)
rationale: Before the manuscript is drafted, the agent audits the claim structure. Answers are recorded; the gate checks completeness. Sources are chapter/item-level references, not page numbers.

items.question: Does every quantitative claim in the manuscript trace to a verified analysis output or extracted value, with the source locator attached?
items.rationale: Unanchored numbers are the dominant manuscript integrity failure; each claim needs its artifact.
items.source: MetaWingman grounding norm; PRISMA 2020 item 20a (results of individual studies)
items.answer_format: claim -> artifact map (file:line or receipt field) for every number

items.question: Does the abstract state the search dates, number of studies and participants, effect estimate with CI, heterogeneity, and certainty — without exceeding what the certainty assessment supports?
items.rationale: Abstracts are the most-read and most-misleading part; conclusion must match GRADE certainty.
items.source: PRISMA 2020 item 2 (structured summary); GRADE handbook (wording of conclusions)
items.answer_format: abstract element checklist + certainty-matched wording check

items.question: Are conclusions worded at the level of the certainty rating, distinguishing evidence of absence from absence of evidence?
items.rationale: "No difference" claims without imprecision context are the classic spin pattern.
items.source: GRADE handbook (interpreting results and drawing conclusions)
items.answer_format: conclusion sentence + its certainty tier + the fallback wording if downgraded

items.question: Are exploratory and sensitivity analyses labeled as such in the text, tables, and figures?
items.rationale: Exploratory results presented as confirmatory mislead readers about prespecification.
items.source: PRISMA 2020 item 13d (methods used for additional analyses)
items.answer_format: labeling rule + audit of every table/figure for compliance

items.question: Does the discussion address limitations including risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision, indirectness, and publication bias as actually assessed — not a generic template paragraph?
items.rationale: Template limitation paragraphs disconnect the discussion from the review's own numbers.
items.answer_format: limitation list keyed to this review's own assessments

items.question: Is the PRISMA 2020 checklist completed against the actual manuscript with item-level page/section locators, not inherited from a template?
items.rationale: A checklist without locators is unverifiable and often copy-pasted.

items.question: Are figures checked for misleading presentation: untruncated axes, named error bars, sample sizes visible, forest plots ordered sensibly, colorblind-safe palette?
items.rationale: Figure-level spin survives text-level checks; visual integrity needs its own pass.
items.source: MetaWingman figure norms (SciPilot-style visual audit); PRISMA 2020 item 20b (synthesis results)

items.question: Is AI assistance disclosed per journal policy: which stages, which tools, with what human verification?
items.rationale: Journals require disclosure; vague disclosure is the MetaWingman reserved-window norm.
items.source: MetaWingman disclosure norm (AI-first execution boundary); ICMJE authorship recommendations
items.answer_format: disclosure paragraph naming stages, tools, and verification

items.question: Does the data/code availability statement name every artifact needed to reproduce the review (data, code, environment, receipts) with access paths?
items.rationale: Reproducibility claims need the artifact list, not a vague 'available on request'.
items.source: PRISMA 2020 item 27 (availability of data, code and other materials)
items.answer_format: artifact list + access path or embargo explanation

items.question: Which single sentence in the draft would a skeptic most challenge, and does its evidence chain hold?
items.rationale: Adversarial self-audit of the load-bearing sentence is the cheapest spin defense.
items.source: MetaWingman AI reviewer panel norm; PRISMA 2020 item 23
items.answer_format: one sentence + its full evidence chain walk-through
